verdict.rationale: x402 documents an HTTP 402 handshake in which the agent signs a payment and the hosted CDP Facilitator verifies it, screens it and submits settlement onchain. The docs specify USDC and any ERC-20/SPL token, a per-network support table (Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, World, Solana), exact/upto/batch schemes, and agentic wallets as the USDC source. Community operators running x402 endpoints, a live Bazaar probe showing USDC listings on Base, and the published npm SDK corroborate it; critics' complaints about KYC or crypto-only rails are opinion, not contradictions. Missing for 10: hands-on or independent verification of an actual end-to-end onchain settlement (the facilitator probe was auth-gated with a 401, so it confirmed access control, not settlement), and the Advanced Trade agent payment path is still 'coming soon'.
